key_insight: Cluster-TNN scales topological deep learning by lifting graph structure locally inside mini-batches instead of materializing the full higher-order domain upfront.
engineering_relevance: This makes higher-order neural networks practical on large graphs by cutting GPU memory demand dramatically while preserving competitive accuracy.
method: Partition the input graph into clusters during preprocessing.
At runtime, sample groups of clusters and reconstruct their induced subgraph as a mini-batch.
Apply the chosen topological lifting only within each mini-batch, retaining intra-batch edges to preserve higher-order structure.
evidence_signal: Across 21 matched full-graph comparisons, Cluster-TNN reduced peak GPU memory in every case, by 83.2% on average, and enabled training on large datasets such as Reddit and OGBN Products.
watch_item: Mini-batch lifting depends on graph partition quality and may not preserve all global higher-order interactions, so performance can be sensitive to how clusters are formed.
paper_title: Batch Before You Lift: Scalable Topological Deep Learning on Large Graphs
